overview: The Pelta-class Frigate is a medical / support frigate whose design philosophy reflects the industrial and strategic priorities of Clone Wars (22–19 BBY). Republic Pelta frigates served as hospital ships and command relays, including the frigate that evacuated Ahsoka Tano's wounded. Production estimates place the class at ~420 units, though wartime losses, capture, and black-market duplication make precise fleet registries unreliable.
history:
Engineering teams first finalized the Pelta-class Frigate blueprints during the political climate of Clone Wars (22–19 BBY). The medical / support frigate was intended to solve specific fleet gaps—whether planetary assault, convoy escort, starfighter superiority, or terror bombardment—and shipwrights iterated hull plates, reactor output, and crew compartments accordingly.

Once deployed, the Pelta-class Frigate appeared in fleet actions that defined its reputation. Republic Pelta frigates served as hospital ships and command relays, including the frigate that evacuated Ahsoka Tano's wounded. Combat logs show crews exploiting the class's strengths while improvising fixes for known weaknesses under fire, a pattern repeated across every major galactic conflict.

As doctrine evolved, rival factions studied captured Pelta-class Frigate hulls. Refit yards duplicated weapons mounts and sensor suites; some variants never appeared in official manifests. Estimated production of ~420 units therefore understates how many similar silhouettes operated under alternate insignia.

Surviving Pelta-class Frigate vessels now sit in museum orbits, mercenary fleets, and scrap worlds. Historians treat the class as a measure of how galactic wars industrialize violence—each hull a factory product that outlived the politicians who ordered it.
significance:
The Pelta-class Frigate demonstrates how medical / support frigate design shapes campaign outcomes. Its layout influenced successor programs and remains a case study in naval academies.

With roughly ~420 units hulls associated with Clone Wars (22–19 BBY), the class became a visual symbol of its faction's reach—recognizable in holonet footage and feared in convoy manifests.

Engineers still debate whether the Pelta-class Frigate prioritized firepower over crew survival; that trade-off defines its legacy in both propaganda and honest after-action reports.
